short.en: Stack the table in two layers

t.en: To fix the counter, the state has to remember one more thing: whether you have the key. Each cell of one table can hold only one number, which can’t keep two kinds of route apart.

This level’s robot, Layercake, stacks the table in two layers: the “no keys” layer holds the routes that haven’t got the key yet, the “red” layer those that have. On every cell it works out both layers.

The cell facts tell the circuit what happens on this layer at this cell. Door shut: there is a door here, but this layer has no key. Routes move on: there is a key here, and routes reaching it pick it up and move to the other layer. Picks up key: there is a key here, and this layer takes in the routes that pick it up.
On the cell with the key, Layercake’s probe reaches up and left on the other layer: that is where those routes come from.

goal.en: Only right or down, and you must have picked up the key before going through a door. Work out the number of valid routes on each map: the end cells of both layers, added up.

how.en: Every cell works out both layers.

title.en: Two layers, each minding its own

body.en: Routes on the “no keys” layer stop at a door; reaching the key cell, they move as a batch to the “red” layer. The “red” layer takes them in at the key cell, and from then on every door is open.
The state went from “which cell” to “which cell, and whether you have the key”: one more thing to remember, one more layer.

hints.en: Count the routes with the Route Counter first, then block the ones that can’t stay on this layer: the door is shut, or the routes move on.
On the cell where the key is picked up, also take in the routes moving over from the other layer: up and left as the probe reaches them, added up.
